segments.arabic:
١١٢٢٧- زينب بنت جحش
الأسدية أم المؤمنين «٣»، زوج النبيّ ﷺ تقدم نسبها في ترجمة أخيها عبد اللَّه وأمها أمية عمة النبيّ ﷺ، تزوّجها النبي ﷺ سنة ثلاث، وقيل سنة خمس، ونزلت بسببها آية الحجاب، وكانت قبله عند مولاه زيد بن حارثة، وفيها نزلت: فَلَمَّا قَضى زَيْدٌ مِنْها وَطَرًا زَوَّجْناكَها [الأحزاب: ٣٧] .
وكان زيد يدعى ابن محمد، فلما نزلت: ادْعُوهُمْ لِآبائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ [الأحزاب: ٥] وتزوّج النبيّ ﷺ امرأته بعده- انتفى ما كان أهل الجاهلية يعتقدونه من أنّ الّذي يتبنّي غيره يصير ابنه، بحيث يتوارثان إلى غير ذلك.
وقد وصفت عائشة زينب بالوصف الجميل في قصة الإفك، وأن اللَّه عصمها بالورع، قالت: وهي التي كانت تساميني من أزواج النبيّ ﷺ، وكانت تفخر على نساء النبيّ ﷺ بأنها بنت عمته، وبأنّ اللَّه زوجها له، وهن زوّجهنّ أولياؤهن.
وفي خبر تزويجها عند ابن سعد من طريق الواقدي بسند مرسل: فبينا رسول اللَّه ﷺ يتحدث عند عائشة إذ أخذته غشية فسرّي عنه وهو يتبسم، ويقول: من يذهب إلى زينب يبشرها؟ وتلا: وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ [الأحزاب: ٣٧] الآية. قالت عائشة: فأخذني ما قرب وما بعد لما يبلغنا من جمالها، وأخرى هي أعظم وأشرق ما صنع لها: زوّجها اللَّه من السماء، وقلت: هي تفخر علينا بهذا.
وبسند ضعيف، عن ابن عباس: لما أخبرت زينب بتزويج رسول اللَّه ﷺ لها سجدت.
ومن طريق عبد الواحد بن أبي عون، قالت زينب: يا رسول اللَّه، إني واللَّه ما أنا
(١) أسد الغابة ت ٦٩٥٠.
(٢) أسد الغابة ت ٦٩٥٣.
(٣) مسند أحمد ٦/ ٣٢٤، طبقات ابن سعد ٨/ ١٠١، طبقات خليفة ٢٣٣، تاريخ خليفة ١٤٩، المعارف ٢١٥، تاريخ الفسوي ٢/ ٧٢٢، المستدرك ٤/ ٢٣، تهذيب الكمال.
segments.english:
11227—Zaynab bint Jahsh

The Asadi woman, Mother of the Believers,[3] and wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Her lineage was given earlier in the entry on her brother Abd Allah, and her mother was Umayma, the paternal aunt of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, married her in the year three, though it is also said that it was in the year five. The verse of the veil was revealed on her account. Before him, she had been married to his freedman Zayd ibn Haritha, and concerning her the following was revealed: “Then, when Zayd had no further need of her, We gave her to you in marriage” [al-Ahzab 33:37].

Zayd used to be called “Ibn Muhammad.” When the following was revealed: “Call them after their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah” [al-Ahzab 33:5], and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, subsequently married the woman who had been his wife, the belief held by the people of the pre-Islamic period was nullified: that a person adopted by another thereby became his son, so that the two inherited from one another, and so forth.

In the account of the slander, Aisha described Zaynab in admirable terms and stated that Allah had protected her through scrupulous piety. She said, “She was the one among the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who vied with me in standing.” Zaynab used to boast before the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that she was the daughter of his paternal aunt and that Allah had married her to him, whereas their guardians had married them to him.

In Ibn Sa'd's report concerning her marriage, transmitted by way of al-Waqidi with a mursal chain: While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was conversing in Aisha's presence, a faintness overtook him. When it passed from him, he was smiling and saying, “Who will go to Zaynab and give her the glad tidings?” He recited: “And when you were saying to the one upon whom Allah had bestowed favor and upon whom you had bestowed favor, ‘Keep your wife and fear Allah’” [al-Ahzab 33:37]—to the end of the verse. Aisha said, “Because of what had reached us concerning her beauty, all manner of thoughts, near and far, assailed me; and there was another matter, greater and more splendid still: what had been done for her—Allah had given her in marriage from heaven. I said, ‘She will boast of this over us.’”

With a weak chain, it is related from Ibn Abbas that when Zaynab was informed of the Messenger of Allah's marriage to her, she prostrated herself.

By way of Abd al-Wahid ibn Abi Awn, Zaynab said, “O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I am not—”

[1] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 6950.

[2] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 6953.

[3] Musnad Ahmad, 6/324; al-Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd, 8/101; al-Tabaqat of Khalifa, 233; Tarikh Khalifa, 149; al-Ma'arif, 215; Tarikh al-Fasawi, 2/722; al-Mustadrak, 4/23; Tahdhib al-Kamal.

segments.arabic:
كإحدى نسائك، ليست امرأة من نسائك إلا زوّجها أبوها أو أخوها أو أهلها غيري، زوّجنيك اللَّه من السماء.
ومن حديث أم سلمة بسند موصول فيه الواقدي- أنها ذكرت زينب فترحّمت عليها، وذكرت ما كان يكون بينها وبين عائشة، فذكرت نحو هذا، قالت أم سلمة: وكانت لرسول اللَّه ﷺ معجبة، وكان يستكثر منها، وكانت صالحة صوّامة قوامة صناعا تصدق بذلك كله على المساكين.
وذكر أبو عمر: كان اسمها برة، فلما دخلت على رسول اللَّه ﷺ سماها زينب. روت عن النبي ﷺ أحاديث، روى عنها ابن أخيها محمد بن عبد اللَّه بن جحش، وأم حبيبة بنت أبي سفيان، وزينب بنت أبي سلمة، ولهم صحبة، وكلثوم بنت المصطلق، ومذكور مولاها، وغيرهم.
قال الواقديّ: ماتت سنة عشرين. وأخرج الطبراني من طريق الشعبي أن عبد الرحمن بن أبزى أخبره أنه صلّى مع عمر على زينب بنت جحش، وكانت أول نساء النبي ﷺ ماتت بعده
. وفي الصحيحين، واللفظ لمسلم، من طريق عائشة بنت طلحة، عن عائشة، قالت: قال رسول اللَّه ﷺ: «أسرعكنّ لحاقا بي أطولكنّ يدا» . قال: فكن يتطاولن أيتهن أطول يدا. قالت: وكانت أطولنا يدا زينب، لأنها كانت تعمل بيدها، وتتصدق.
ومن طريق يحيى بن سعيد، عن عمرة، عن عائشة نحو المرفوع، قالت عائشة: فكنا إذا اجتمعنا في بيت إحدانا بعد وفاة رسول اللَّه ﷺ نمدّ أيدينا في الجدار نتطاول، فلم نزل نفعل ذلك حتى توفيت زينب بنت جحش، وكانت امرأة قصيرة، ولم تكن بأطولنا، فعرفنا حينئذ أنّ النبيّ ﷺ إنما أراد طول اليد بالصدقة، وكانت زينب امرأة صناع اليدين، فكانت تدبغ وتخرز وتتصدق به في سبيل.
وروينا في «القطعيّات»، من طريق شهر بن حوشب، عن عبد اللَّه بن شداد، عن ميمونة بنت الحارث، قالت، كان رسول اللَّه ﷺ يقسم ما أفاء اللَّه عليه في رهط من المهاجرين، فتكلّمت زينب بنت جحش، فانتهرها عمر، فقال رسول اللَّه ﷺ: «خلّ عنها يا عمر، فإنّها أوّاهة» «١» .
وأخرج ابن سعد بسند فيه الواقديّ، عن القاسم بن محمد، قال: قالت زينب حين حضرتها الوفاة: إني قد أعددت كفني، وإنّ عمر سيبعث إلي بكفن، فتصدقوا بأحدهما، إن استطعتم أن تتصدقوا بحقوي فافعلوا.
(١) أورده السيوطي بنحوه في الدر المنثور ٣/ ١٨٦.
segments.english:
…like any one of your wives. There is no woman among your wives whom her father, brother, or family did not marry to you, except me: Allah married me to you from heaven.

In a report from Umm Salama, with a continuous chain containing al-Waqidi, she mentioned Zaynab and asked Allah to have mercy upon her. She mentioned what used to occur between her and Aisha, relating something similar to this. Umm Salama said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, admired her, and he desired much of her company. She was righteous, much given to fasting and night prayer, and skilled in handicrafts; she gave everything she earned thereby in charity to the poor.”

Abu Umar mentioned: Her name was Barra, but when she came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he named her Zaynab. She transmitted hadiths from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Those who transmitted from her included her nephew Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan, and Zaynab bint Abi Salama—all of whom had Companionship—as well as Kulthum bint al-Mustaliq, her client Madhkur, and others.

Al-Waqidi said: She died in the year 20. Al-Tabarani related through al-Sha'bi that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza informed him that he performed the funeral prayer with Umar over Zaynab bint Jahsh, and she was the first of the Prophet's wives to die after him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, with Muslim's wording, through Aisha bint Talha, from Aisha, she said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The one of you who will join me soonest is the one with the longest hand.” He said: They therefore began comparing their reach to see which of them had the longest hand. She said: “The one of us with the longest hand was Zaynab, because she used to work with her hands and give in charity.”

Through Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Amra, from Aisha, there is a similar report attributed to the Prophet. Aisha said: “Whenever we gathered in the house of one of us after the death of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, we would extend our hands against the wall and compare their lengths. We continued doing that until Zaynab bint Jahsh died. She was a short woman and was not the tallest of us. We then realized that by ‘length of hand’ the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had meant charity. Zaynab was a woman skilled with her hands: she would tan hides and stitch leather, and would give the proceeds in charity for the cause [of Allah].”

We transmitted in al-Qat'iyyat, through Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymuna bint al-Harith, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was distributing what Allah had bestowed upon him as fay' among a group of the Emigrants. Zaynab bint Jahsh spoke, and Umar rebuked her. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Leave her alone, Umar, for she is deeply humble and much given to supplication.”¹

Ibn Sa'd related, with a chain containing al-Waqidi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: When death approached Zaynab, she said: “I have prepared my shroud, but Umar will send me another shroud. Give one of the two away in charity; and if you can give away even my waist-wrapper in charity, then do so.”

¹ Al-Suyuti cited a similar report in al-Durr al-Manthur, 3/186.

segments.arabic:
ومن وجه آخر، عن عمرة، قالت: بعث عمر بخمسة أثواب يتخيرها ثوبا ثوبا من الحراني، فكفنت منها، وتصدقت عنها أختها حمنة بكفنها الّذي كانت أعدته.
قالت عمرة: فسمعت عائشة تقول: لقد ذهبت حميدة متعبدة مفزع اليتامى والأرامل.
وأخرج بسند فيه الواقديّ عن محمد بن كعب: كان عطاء زينب بنت جحش اثني عشر ألفا لم تأخذه إلا عاما واحدا، فجعلت تقول: اللَّهمّ لا يدركني هذا المال من قابل فإنه فتنة، ثم قسمته في أهل رحمها وفي أهل الحاجة، فبلغ عمر، فقال: هذه امرأة يراد بها خير، فوقف عليها، وأرسل بالسلام، وقال: بلغني ما فرقت. فأرسل بألف درهم تستبقيها، فسلكت به ذلك المسلك.
وتقدم في ترجمة برة بنت رافع في القسم الرابع من حرف الباء الموحدة نحو هذه القصة مطولا.
قال الواقديّ: تزوّجها النبيّ- ﷺ وهي بنت خمس وثلاثين سنة، وماتت سنة عشرين، وهي بنت خمسين، ونقل عن عمر بن عثمان الحجبي أنها عاشت ثلاثا وخمسين.
segments.english:
By another route, from Amra, who said: Umar sent five garments that he had selected one garment at a time from al-Harrani. Some of them were used to shroud her, and her sister Hamna gave away in charity on her behalf the shroud that Zaynab had prepared.

Amra said: I heard Aisha say, “A praiseworthy, devout woman has indeed departed—the refuge of orphans and widows.”

He also transmitted, with a chain containing al-Waqidi, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: Zaynab bint Jahsh’s stipend was twelve thousand, and she received it for only one year. She kept saying, “O Allah, do not let this money reach me next year, for it is a temptation.” She then distributed it among her relatives and people in need. When Umar heard of this, he said, “This is a woman for whom good is intended.” He went to her, sent her greetings, and said, “I have heard about what you distributed.” He then sent her one thousand dirhams so that she might retain them, but she disposed of them in the same way.

An extended version of an account similar to this appeared above in the biography of Barra bint Rafi, in the fourth section of the singly dotted letter ba.

Al-Waqidi said: The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—married her when she was thirty-five years old, and she died in the year 20, aged fifty. It is related from Umar ibn Uthman al-Hajabi that she lived for fifty-three years.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش
names.english: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Jahsh

unresolved.explanation: The expression may denote a person known as al-Harrani, possibly a merchant, or Harrani cloth or goods. The supplied Urdu and collateral witnesses do not reproduce this sentence. The final translation therefore retains al-Harrani without specifying the referent.
